chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali al-Jarmi from them(2) from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him: A man performed Tawaf and did not know whether he performed seven (circuits) or eight (circuits). He said: 'He prays two Rak'at.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they are unsure whether they completed 7 or 8 rounds of Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the uncertainty in the number of Tawaf circuits is resolved by performing two additional Rak'at, reflecting the Shia principle of relying on the 'original state' (al-asl) when doubt arises between two possibilities. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the validity of worship over rigid perfectionism when specific evidence is absent. It serves as a key precedent for handling minor doubts in ritual acts, distinguishing between obligatory and recommended acts in the context of Hajj and Umrah.
